Application Materials.content:
For international students, as part of the application process, you'll need to submit:
- School or college transcripts/certificates
- University transcripts and certified translations if applicable
- Degree certificates
- Evidence of English Language proficiency, unless you're a national of a [majority English speaking country](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/international/applying/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/majority-english-speaking-countries/)
- Personal statement outlining your learning ambitions.
For external intercalating applicants, what you'll need:
- School or college transcripts/certificates
- University transcripts and certified translations if applicable
- Degree certificates
- Evidence of English Language proficiency, unless you're a national of a [majority English speaking country](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/international/applying/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/majority-english-speaking-countries/)
- Personal statement (**500 word limit**) including why you want to study on this course and evidence of experience in this field.

Interview Requirements.content:
Admissions staff may consider a range of factors in assessing suitability for their programmes including, but not limited to, interviews, work experience, assessment of a piece of written work, etc.
For campus-based programmes, the length of time it will take to process an application and arrive at a decision will depend both on whether the academic School concerned requires additional information or uses additional selection procedures, such as an interview. Depending on the programme, an application may be considered on the basis of the information provided in the application form and supporting documentation, or the applicant may be required to attend for interview or provide additional evidence of relevant work experience or submit a piece of work or an essay for consideration by the selector.
For some programmes, decisions are made on the basis of the information provided by the applicant only; in other cases, applicants may be called for interview. In some Schools, interviews may be used only for candidates who have unusual or non-standard qualifications, in order to give them an opportunity to demonstrate that they have the skills and knowledge required for them to thrive on their chosen programme of study. Where appropriate, applicants may be interviewed via telephone, Zoom, MS Teams or Skype.
For international applicants, to ensure that the University complies with relevant United Kingdom legislation and immigration regulations, the University may choose to undertake additional checks during the admissions process and this may be post offer. These include, but are not exclusive to, credibility interviews, financial checks, and qualification checks. These may be conducted directly by the University or an approved third party. Applicants who are unsuccessful during any additional checks will not be issued a CAS and are at risk of having their academic offer withdrawn.

Application Deadlines.content:
Start date: [**September 2026**](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/courses/data-science-ai-for-health-msc/2026). Starts on: **28 September 2026**.
International students: Apply for this course by **21 August 2026**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- We accept a **2:2 honours degree from a UK university**, or an **equivalent academic qualification from a similar non-UK institution**.
- Applicants can hold a degree in **any subject area** but should be able to demonstrate evidence of previous experience of **quantitative analysis in statistics and/or computer science** (for example, as part of an undergraduate module or relevant work experience).
- This programme is also open to **intercalating students on clinical programmes**.
- Specifically, this master’s programme is suitable if you hold a **2.2 degree from a UK University (or equivalent)**. Your first degree could be in any subject, as long as you are able to evidence previous experience of quantitative skills, for example, at least one module in your degree in **statistics, computer science or mathematics**.
- Applicants may come from backgrounds including Statistics, Mathematics, Computer science, Data science, Biomedical sciences, Psychology, Public health, Health sciences, or Clinical research.
- For students who do not hold a first degree in a relevant subject area, the page refers to the [MSc Data Science & AI for Health Innovation (Conversion)](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/courses/data-science-for-health-conversion-msc), designed for students wishing to move into the field of data science irrespective of their background and previous training.
- **China (mainland) applicants:** taught master's applications with a bachelor's degree from a **recognised Chinese university**, with overall average academic grades between **65% to 78%** depending on the level/tier of Chinese university, will generally be considered for admissions onto taught master's programmes. Some courses require higher entry requirements.

Program Overview.content:
Qualification type: MSc. Study mode: Full-time or part-time. Duration: 12 months full-time or 24 months part-time.
Advance your expertise in statistics, machine learning and responsible AI for healthcare innovation. The MSc Data Science and AI for Health Innovation prepares students to tackle real-world healthcare challenges using advanced statistical methods, machine learning and artificial intelligence.
Healthcare is being transformed by data science, artificial intelligence and digital technologies. From electronic health records and wearable devices to AI-driven diagnostics and public health surveillance, healthcare systems now generate vast amounts of data with enormous potential to improve patient care and health outcomes. This programme combines advanced statistical analysis, machine learning, artificial intelligence and computational methods to explore how health data science can drive meaningful healthcare innovation.
Designed around flexibility and student choice, the programme allows students to tailor their studies around their own interests and career ambitions. Students can specialise in areas such as prediction modelling, artificial intelligence, machine learning, casual inference and healthcare evaluation while developing analytical, computational and professional skills.
The programme has strong links with the [Civic Health Innovation Labs (CHIL)](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/civic-health-innovation-labs/), an internationally recognised multidisciplinary research centre based at the University of Liverpool. CHIL brings together experts from academia, the NHS, local government, charities and industry to develop responsible approaches to data use and AI for health and society. Students have opportunities to engage with dissertation projects linked to areas such as healthcare data analytics, digital health, public health informatics and community health innovation, contributing to cutting-edge research with real-world impact.
The programme is designed for students with prior quantitative experience who wish to develop advanced expertise in health data science and artificial intelligence, and is also suitable for professionals seeking to strengthen their analytical and computational skills for careers in healthcare, research and innovation. It is also open to intercalating students on clinical programmes.
The curriculum combines core foundations in health data science with flexible specialist pathways in statistics, machine learning and artificial intelligence. Students develop expertise in using health data to better understand disease and improve healthcare; applying data science approaches to real-world healthcare challenges; statistical modelling, inference and prediction; machine learning and artificial intelligence for healthcare innovation; causal inference and healthcare intervention evaluation; managing and interpreting complex health data; computational and programming methods for health research; responsible and ethical approaches to AI and healthcare data use; communication of analytical findings; collaborative and interdisciplinary working; and designing and completing an independent health data science research project.
The programme has a blended format with a mix of face-to-face lectures, workshops and practical sessions. Full-time students complete the programme in three semesters and part-time students complete it in six semesters. Work towards the dissertation module runs across the length of the programme, with the dissertation completed in semester three.
Teaching takes place within a welcoming and collaborative academic community supported by staff with expertise across statistics, health data science, artificial intelligence and healthcare research. Teaching is enriched by guest lecturers and research collaborations connected to organisations including the NHS, industry and CHIL.
Graduates from the MSc Data Science and AI for Health Innovation are equipped with advanced statistical, computational and analytical skills sought across healthcare, industry and research. The programme prepares graduates for careers including healthcare analytics, NHS data science, pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, clinical trials and health research, public health and epidemiology, digital health innovation, AI-driven healthcare technologies, healthcare evaluation and policy, and academic and methodological research. Graduates may work within hospitals, government agencies, research organisations, pharmaceutical companies, healthcare technology companies and innovation-focused startups. The programme also provides preparation for doctoral study and research careers in health data science, statistics and artificial intelligence.

Cost of Attendance.content:
UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) requires that you have **£10,539 per academic year**, equivalent to **£1,171 per month for nine months**, to cover daily living expenses including accommodation, food and local travel. The £10,539 figure is based on a nine-month stay in the UK. If staying for 12 months, you are likely to need at least **£14,052** to cover living costs, based on the UKVI's minimum monthly amount.
The University estimates total monthly living expenses of **£900-£1,350** based on feedback from current international undergraduate and master's students. Typical monthly costs include:
- University halls accommodation, including electricity, gas, water, and Wi-Fi: **£688-£1,120 per month**
- Private accommodation: **£400-£700 per month**
- Household bills for private accommodation, including electricity, gas, water, and Wi-Fi: **£50-£200 per month**
- Travel and transport: **£20-£80 per month**
- Food and other household necessities: **£150-£400 per month**
- Mobile phone bill: **£15-£50 per month**
- Television Licence: **£14.12 per month** or **£169.50 for the full year**
- Socialising and entertainment: **£50-£200 per month**
- Study costs, including books and photocopying: **£10-£30 per month**
- Gym membership, based on University Sports Centre: **from £22 per month**

Financial Aid.content:
All or part of your tuition fees can be [funded by external sponsorship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/feespayment/tuition/external-sponsorship/).
We’re showing the scholarships available to students from **United Kingdom**. We offer a range of scholarships and bursaries that could help pay your tuition and living expenses.
- [Graduate Loyalty Scholarship – UK](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/graduate-loyalty-scholarship-uk/): UK or Republic of Ireland students who completed an undergraduate degree at the University of Liverpool could receive a **£1,500 tuition fee discount**, subject to the full eligibility criteria. This scholarship will be awarded to all eligible students.
- [The Salters’ Fellowship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/the-salters-fellowship/): students who have graduated with an undergraduate degree in Chemistry and accepted a place on a master's course could be entitled to a **£10,000 contribution towards tuition fees**. The master's can be in a range of subject areas and is not restricted to Chemistry; available to one student per academic year who's considered to be from a widening participation background.
- [Bracken Scholarship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/paying-for-your-studies/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/bracken-scholarship/): open to two UK students in the **2026/27 academic year** and worth **£5,000**. Students must be studying a postgraduate course at the University of Liverpool; those on data science or coding courses may be given priority.
- [Health Data Research UK Master’s Degree Scholarships](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/paying-for-your-studies/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/health-data-research-masters-scholarship/): joining our Health Data Science MSc? UK students could be eligible to apply for **£10,000 of funding** and the opportunity to conduct a research project with one of HDRUK’s partner organisations. Partners include Diabetes UK and Alzheimer's Research UK.
- [John Lennon Memorial Scholarship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/paying-for-your-studies/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/john-lennon-memorial-scholarship/): UK students either born in or with strong family connections to Merseyside could be eligible to apply for a fee discount of up to **£4,500**. Applicants need to demonstrate an active interest in global, community and environmental issues.
- [Sport Liverpool Performance Programme](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/paying-for-your-studies/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/sport-liverpool-performance-programme/): applicants can receive tailored training support to enhance sporting performance, including benefits from bespoke strength and conditioning training to physiotherapy sessions and one-to-one nutritional advice.

Multiple Applications.content: Please note that you can accept only one unconditional offer. If you have been made unconditional offers for more than one programme, you will need to choose one to accept. The Admissions Team will then decline any other offers.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: If for an unforeseen reason you are not able to take up the place of an offer for the academic year you have applied for, you can defer your offer of a place for **one academic year**. You can only defer your studies once. If you request to defer your offer, and then ask to defer again the following year, the Admissions Team will not be able to process the request, and a new application will have to be submitted. You may only request a deferral up until **31 October** for the following year's entry. After this date a deferral may not be possible. To request a deferral for postgraduate taught programmes, please use the [postgraduate application tracker](https://pgapptracker.liverpool.ac.uk/).
